A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same function-vector study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–K are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original task-accuracy and causal-intervention experiments comparing instruction and demonstration function vectors across Llama and OLMo models, with additional analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds OLMo joint-intervention and mixed-head evaluations in Appendices G.3 and I.2.

M1.justification: The FV extraction procedure, three uninformative-prompt construction methods, head selection, and additive interventions remain unchanged. Joint interventions and mixed head/activation FVs already appeared in v1; evaluating them on OLMo introduces no new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 50-task collection, exclusions, instruction sources, and zero-shot/shuffled-demonstration scenarios. The added OLMo analyses retain this coverage. MMLU and BBH are newly mentioned as future evaluation possibilities, not evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: Within OLMo evaluations, v3 adds joint-FV and mixed head/activation alternatives to the existing single-FV comparisons (Figures 13–15 and 29). These alternatives were already evaluated for Llama in v1. The uninformative-prompt and no-intervention baselines remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 expands the reported OLMo evaluation design to joint and heterogeneous interventions, applying existing fixed-depth, empirically optimal-depth, and matched/mismatched evaluation procedures. This is an extension of evaluated model–intervention combinations; the original splits, accuracy metric, sample counts, and head counts are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices G.3 and I.2 extend tests of joint-FV benefits and head-source asymmetry to the four OLMo checkpoints, including depth sensitivity and mismatched evaluations. These provide additional checks of existing findings. The earlier double-FV, low-causal-head, instruction-length, and baseline-choice analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify one run per model-task-setting and report standard errors of the mean. v3's checklist reiterates SEM reporting and the absence of significance tests; it introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or repeated-seed evaluation.

E6.justification: v3 adds OLMo joint-intervention accuracies and heterogeneous-FV results, showing benefits from combining FVs and generally lower accuracy with mixed head/activation sources. Existing plotted results and numerical Tables 6–8 are retained. Some single-FV panels in the new figures redisplay OLMo results already present in v1.

T1.justification: The task-conditioned activation, causal indirect effect, FV, and baseline-sampling definitions in Section 2 and Appendix B are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical results or proofs, and v3 adds none.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion narrow the conclusion from different presentations not inducing a common task representation to not inducing one through function vectors. This limits the headline claim to the studied representation method. The five principal findings in Table 1 remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds possible explanations involving Llama distillation and the fraction of selected heads, connects instruction mechanisms to post-training depth alignment, and proposes multilayer steering and head-based prompt diagnostics. These are interpretive or speculative extensions; the main limitations already acknowledged in v1 remain.

D1.justification: The new checklist states that supplementary code includes a ZIP archive, environment setup instructions, and example experiment commands, with public release planned. v1 lacks this disclosure. Existing implementation, hardware, and compute details remain unchanged; the supplied PDFs cannot verify the archive itself.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds references on task vectors and prompt sensitivity, including Han, Li, Min, Sclar, and Su, and distinguishes residual-token, per-layer, and attention-head representation approaches. Section 5.1 adds MMLU and BBH references as future directions. The central positioning relative to prior FV work remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose revisions and explanatory additions, adds acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist, and inserts OLMo appendix subsections. Author affiliations and publication text also change. The main narrative, five-finding organization, and overall appendix structure remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds four multipanel figures, numbered 13–15 and 29, using the existing visual style. Retained appendix figures are renumbered and reflowed, and Table 7 moves relative to the Appendix J heading. Existing figures and table structures otherwise remain visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added OLMo joint-intervention and mixed-head analyses extend support for important findings beyond the Llama experiments previously reported for those comparisons. Qualifying the headline conclusion as specific to function vectors better aligns it with the evidence and v1's existing limitations. These are useful, limited gains; the task coverage, single-run design, and underlying method remain unchanged.
